title: Counting Pump Insulin for Infusion Sets — Insulin Pump Program Pharmacy Coordination Note
content:
For an infusion-set refill on an Insulin Pump Program, the counting of the customer's pump insulin follows the customer's Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program — the customer's active insulin pharmacy program whose delivery method is insulin pump:

| The customer's insulin pharmacy programs | Effect on the standard counting |
|---|---|
| The active pump-delivery program is on any tier other than the Insulin Pharmacy Medicare Part B Pump Insulin Program | the standard counting is replaced with its rapid-acting 10 mL vial dispensing (insulin aspart and insulin lispro 10 mL vials), each vial holding 1000 units of insulin (the vial insulin) |
| The customer holds no active pump-delivery insulin pharmacy program | no pump insulin is counted |
| Otherwise (the active pump-delivery program is the Insulin Pharmacy Medicare Part B Pump Insulin Program) | the standard counting from J1817 dispensing at 50 units of insulin per billing unit stands |

An insulin pharmacy program that is not active, or whose delivery method is not insulin pump, is not a source of pump insulin for this purpose.

## Worked conversions (hypothetical dispensing records)

- A pump-delivery program on another tier dispensed 3 rapid-acting 10 mL vials: 3 multiplied by 1000 is 3,000 units of insulin.
- A Part B pump insulin program dispensed 60 J1817 billing units: 60 multiplied by 50 is 3,000 units of insulin.
- A customer whose only insulin pharmacy program delivers by pen: no pump insulin is counted.
